# Vote simulation: the odds the agenda passes the 2029-30 Congress

*Generated by index/tools/votes-model.py from the ledger and index/data/inputs/votes-bills.csv and votes-senate.csv (4,000 simulated Congresses per scenario, fixed seed). Do not edit by hand. Every vote parameter is the war-game simulator's or an estimate (each row's basis is in votes-bills.csv); the Senate roster is the war game's mid-2026 map and is re-baselined after the Nov 3 election. Read the results as relative odds for comparing paths and packages, not forecasts.*

**Bottom line (53 seats, the middle of D1's 52-54; 221 House seats).** Under graduated cloture (F, decided) the rules change is adopted in 73% of simulated Congresses. Some version of each reconciliation bill passes the Senate in 100% (R1), 100% (R2) and 100% (R3) of them, but as written only 3%, 0% and 38%: the rest pass after provisions are dropped. The provisions most often dropped are REV-R2B (R2 revenue on rates and corporations (G3, G5, G10, C18, C20, C38-C41, C43); missing from 82% of passing versions), REV-R1 (R1 revenue: corporate rate, foreign income, 2025-cut reversal (G1, G7, G9); missing from 75% of passing versions), REV-R2A (R2 revenue on wealth: mark-to-market, gains at death, estate tax (G11, G6, C35); missing from 70% of passing versions). Of 21 regular-order bills, about 11.5 are enacted on average under F conditional on reaching the floor (the legacy calendar filter is not applied), against 2.1 under the carve-out fallback (G) and 0.1 with no rules change.

**Integrated calendar:** scenario demand, capacity, dated completion and delivery opportunity are reported separately in index/calendar-scenarios.md and index/calendar-delivery-opportunities.md. The legacy 163-day allocation is a historical diagnostic only and does not zero out the default vote estimates. No scenario probability weights or independence assumption are used to combine these models.

## By rules path

**CAP-7S routing assumption (Oct 21):** the full multi-year surge targets R1, immediately available on enactment. Vote results assume reconciliation eligibility, not a Byrd/jurisdiction certification, including SSA scope. FY2029 cash costing is separate.

53 seats. Packages need a simple majority whatever the path; the path decides cloture for regular-order bills and the appropriations omnibus.

| Path | Rules change adopted | Regular-order bills enacted (of 21), conditional on floor access | Legacy calendar-filtered diagnostic | Appropriations omnibus enacted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F, graduated cloture (decided) | 73% | 11.5 | 10.1 | 73% |
| C, talking filibuster (opening offer) | 84% | 13.1 | 8.9 | 83% |
| E, majority cloture (upper bound) | 72% | 11.3 | 10.6 | 72% |
| G, democracy carve-out (fallback) | 92% | 2.1 | 2.1 | 1% |
| No rules change | — | 0.1 | 0.1 | 1% |

## Reconciliation packages

A package needs 50 senators plus the Vice President and gets no Republican votes. As written: no provision draws an objection that costs the majority. Some version: leadership drops the provisions holdouts object to until a majority holds (see the provisions table below for what survives).

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | 7 | 3% | 100% | 98% | 98% |
| R2 | 19 | 0% | 100% | 95% | 95% |
| R3 | 6 | 38% | 100% | 99% | 99% |

## Limits

- Objection rates are the war game's archetype rates where a bill maps to one, otherwise estimates; nothing here is polling or whip counts.
- Objections are independent across senators and bills; real holdouts move together, so the packages' odds are probably too low at the extremes and too high in the middle.
- Trimming ignores the Byrd rule: a package that drops revenue but keeps permanent spending would fail the out-year test, so a dropped revenue provision means replacement revenue or a smaller program, which the vehicle checker on the roadmap will test.
- DEM-1 must begin floor consideration by March 2029; SS has a spring-2030 target. Capacity reservations protect them but do not validate these dated deadlines. Other priorities can move early/in parallel. Seasonal target labels do not select a passage month.
- Byrd challenges, amendments, conference and timing inside the year are not modeled; the House model is the war game's frontliner drag (for a package, its most exposed provision).
- The roster is the war game's mid-2026 map; re-baseline it in votes-senate.csv after Nov 3.
